 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. On Saturday, the Dallas Stars will look to bounce back in a big way, after suffering a lopsided 8-3 defeat at the hands of the Winnipeg Jets on Thursday. Their next challenge comes against an Eastern Conference opponent in the Buffalo Sabres, who will be looking to take advantage of a Dallas team eager to get back on track.
 Despite Thursday's setback, the Stars have been playing some excellent hockey recently, winning eight of their last 12 games.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Dallas got the better of Buffalo in their first encounter this season back in October, cruising to a convincing 4-0 shutout victory on the road. The Sabres will undoubtedly have revenge on their minds as they look to even the season series.
 Buffalo enters the contest having dropped four of their last five games, setting the stage for an intriguing matchup between two teams looking to tighten things up defensively. The Sabres have struggled in their own zone all season, ranking fifth-worst in the NHL with an average of 3.53 goals against per game.
 Defensive issues have also become a growing concern for Dallas, despite its blue line typically being one of the team's biggest strengths. Injuries have taken a significant toll, with Lian Bichsel and Kyle Capobianco sidelined. Miro Heiskanen was spotted at Saturday's morning skate but is not expected to suit up either. As a result, AHL call-ups Trey Taylor and Kyle Burroughs are expected to fill out the Stars' bottom defensive pairing.
 The injury troubles have clearly made an impact with Dallas surrendering 31 goals over its last eight games, the sixth-most in the NHL during that stretch. The Stars will need a much stronger defensive effort if they hope to get back in the win column against a Buffalo team hungry for redemption.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement On the offensive side, all eyes will be on Jamie Benn, who enters Saturday's matchup just one point away from reaching the prestigious 1,000-point milestone. The Stars captain will have an opportunity to join an exclusive group in franchise history, adding another storyline to an already important game for Dallas.
